headline: Asia is bouncing and oil stays near $98, so the night was good for India. But after an 8.6% week, with weekly expiry today and a holiday tomorrow, expect a flat-to-higher start and choppy trade near 25,000.

mood.label: Positive
mood.why: The dashboard scores +33 (mildly bullish), but only 2 of its 4 direction checks agree, and fear (India VIX) is high and rising. Overnight data as of 08:48 IST.

key_points.text: Overnight: Asia is rebounding after last week's tech crash (Japan **+3.4%**, Taiwan +6%, Korea +1.7%), and US futures are up about 0.6%.
Foreign investors (FIIs) bought **₹45,960 crore** of Indian shares last week, their biggest buying spree in years, as money left expensive US tech stocks.
My call: a mild continuation is a bit more likely than a pullback today, but with **low confidence**. The market is very stretched and the Sunday Diwali session faded from 25,070 to 24,986.
India VIX (the fear gauge) rose to **18.4** while prices rose, and the market shuts tomorrow. Some traders may close bets today.

sections.title: What changed overnight
sections.summary: The night brought mostly better news, which supports last week's rally rather than working against it.

points.text: GIFT Nifty (the overnight pointer for India's open) was at **25,080** at 7:50 am, about 90 points above Nifty's 24,986 close. An earlier quote was 25,006, so the signal is mild.
Asia is bouncing after a 4.6% fall last week: Nikkei **+3.4%**, Taiwan +6.0%, Kospi +1.7%. The global tech panic looks calmer.
US stocks rose Friday (Nasdaq +1.1%) and S&P futures are **up 0.6%** this morning, after the S&P's worst week since April 2025.
Brent crude is flat at **$98** after a 16% fall last week, as Trump said new strikes on Iran are unlikely while talks go on. Cheap oil helps India.
Gold rose **1.3%** (some investors still want safety) and the US 10-year rate edged up to 4.88%. A small warning sign.

sections.title: Bounce or continuation?
sections.summary: After a huge up week, I lean toward a mild continuation today, with low confidence and a real chance of a pause.

points.text: For continuation: FIIs bought ₹13,750 crore on Friday, about **3.5 times** their normal day, and overnight news is good.
FIIs hold only **24.6%** of index-futures bets as bets on a rise (10.5% a week ago). Many bets on a fall remain, and closing them could push prices up.
For a pause: Nifty is **7.5% above** its 20-day average, very stretched. The Sunday Diwali session also faded from 25,070 to 24,986, so sellers wait near 25,000.
What would prove me wrong: Nifty falling below **24,800** early, or Asia giving up its gains.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.summary: The trend has turned up, but the dashboard's other checks are only lukewarm.

points.text: Nifty is above its 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (23,240 / 23,264 / 23,991). Price trend score: **+1**.
Friday futures rose 2% while open bets fell 2.9%: traders closing bets on a fall, not fresh buying. Positioning score: **+1.25**.
Option sellers are split around 25,000–25,100 (score +0.05), and the put-call ratio (bets on a fall vs bets on a rise) is 1.47, near 'overheated' 1.5 (score +0.3). Total bias: **+33**.
Option prices are expensive: the fear gauge is at the **84th percentile** of the past year and rising, so big swings either way are likely.

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.summary: Foreign money is pouring in while Indian funds are selling into it.

points.text: FIIs bought **₹45,960 crore** in November so far, more than all of October's selling, as money left costly AI stocks for India.
Domestic funds sold **₹24,897 crore** this month, taking profits. They may not buy the dips if the rally runs too far.
Late October, FIIs bought telecom (**₹11,065 crore**) and IT, and sold FMCG, autos, oil & gas and metals (NSDL).

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.summary: Oil and the rupee help India a lot, but US interest rates are a growing worry.

points.text: Brent near **$98** cuts India's import bill and inflation; the rupee gained 52 paise on Friday to 93.89 per dollar.
US markets now expect a **Fed rate hike** (6-month US bills pay 4.23% vs the Fed's 3.88%). Higher US rates can pull money out of India.
US fear is still high (US VIX **25.6**). If the AI selloff returns, Indian IT is exposed: Infosys's US shares fell 2.3% Friday.

sections.title: Company results
sections.summary: Big-company results in the last week were mostly strong.

points.text: Strong last week: Hindalco profit **+59%**, Titan +114%, ONGC +47%, Bharti Airtel +24%, SBI +20% vs last year.
ITC's profit fell **18.5%** despite 44% higher revenue: weak by the dashboard's rule.
No Nifty 50 company reports today. Eicher, Grasim and Tata Motors (cars) report on **13 Nov**.

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.summary: This week has two big inflation reports and a holiday break.

points.text: Today 15:30: **weekly expiry**, moved up because Tuesday is a holiday. Expect sharp late swings.
Tue 19:00 IST: **US inflation** data while India is shut. A hot number raises Fed hike fears; India reacts Wednesday.
Thu 16:00: **India inflation**, ahead of the RBI meeting on 4 Dec.
A setback in US–Iran talks could push oil back above **$100** fast.

levels.note: Option sellers defend 25,500 above and 24,500 below; a close above 25,500 would mean the rally is breaking new ground, while a close below 24,500 would undo most of Thursday's jump.

watch.text: Opening level vs 25,000. Holding above it after the Sunday fade would back the continuation call.
Asian markets through the morning: if Japan and Taiwan give up gains, expect India to weaken too.
Last half hour of weekly expiry before a holiday: watch for sharp moves near 25,000 and 25,100.
Evening FII/DII data: a big FII buy again keeps the rally fuel going; a switch to selling would be a warning.
Tue 10 Nov: US inflation data, with India shut. It sets Wednesday's tone.

bottom_line: The night was mildly good: Asia is bouncing, US futures are up and oil stays cheap, so today should open flat to slightly higher. The dashboard leans bullish (+33) but only 2 of 4 checks agree, fear is rising, and Nifty is stretched after an 8.6% week. Record FII buying is the main support while Indian funds sell into it. The main risk is traders closing bets before the holiday and US inflation data, turning today into a dip below 24,800.
